p2.key:
(i) A mass spectrometer. Steps in order (any five):

  • vaporise the gallium sample and inject it into the evacuated chamber;
  • ionise: a beam of high-energy electrons knocks electrons off atoms → positive ions;
  • accelerate the positive ions with charged plates (electric field);
  • deflect the ions with a magnetic field perpendicular to their path;
  • ions of different mass are deflected by different amounts (lighter ions more);
  • detect: the detector records each mass and its abundance.

(ii) Ga-69: 31 protons, 38 neutrons (31 electrons); Ga-71: 31 protons, 40 neutrons.

Ar = (60 × 69 + 40 × 71)/100 = 69.8

Note: modern IB does not examine the workings of the mass spectrometer, only interpreting spectra.

Diagram with labels in the correct order:

  • vaporization (sample vaporized/injected)
  • ionization (electron gun / beam of high-energy electrons)
  • acceleration (oppositely charged plates / electric field)
  • deflection (magnetic field)
  • detection (detector)

Marks for labels, correct order, and a sketch showing ionization, acceleration and deflection.

(i) Only charged particles can be accelerated by an electric field and then deflected by a magnetic field (by an amount that depends on m/z). Without mentioning the fields, only 1 mark.

(ii) The low pressure stops the ions colliding with air molecules, which would deflect them and give false readings.

p2.key: Ar is a weighted average of the isotope masses. Cobalt has a greater proportion of heavier isotopes (more neutrons) than nickel, so its Ar is higher even though it has fewer protons.
Co has Z = 27, so Co2+ has 27 protons and 25 electrons; losing 2 electrons does not change the number of protons.

(i) Let x = % of 121Sb: [121x + 123(100 − x)] ÷ 100 = 121.75. This gives 12 300 − 2x = 12 175, so x = 62.5. Answer: 121Sb 62.5%, 123Sb 37.5%.

(ii) The ions are deflected by the magnetic field by an amount that depends on m/z, so the lighter 121Sb+ ions are deflected more than 123Sb+. The detector turns ion arrivals into an electric current. The ratio of the peak heights gives the abundance ratio (62.5 : 37.5).

(iii) Neutrons = 121 − 51 = 70.
